pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Dark contiguous regions exhibit high edge angularity with sharp pixel-level gradients. Geometry is characterized by irregular, interlocking polygonal shapes on the mid-flank, transitioning to smaller, more fragmented and stellate forms towards the posterior and lower neck regions.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Light-colored corridors form a continuous, interconnected topological graph. Junction nodes are primarily tri-radial (Y-junctions) and quadri-radial. Corridor pixel thickness remains relatively uniform across the mid-flank with slight narrowing at junction nodes.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: The mane along the upper neck presents a high-frequency, low-amplitude jagged 1D silhouette against the background, created by individual hair-cluster protrusions.
dorsal_ridge_profile.contour_gaps: Structural discontinuities in the mane profile are visible at the dorsal-cervical junction, specifically where avian subjects are perched.

focal_dorsal_anomalies.chronic_feeding_lesions: A localized area of brownish textural disruption and hyper-pigmentation is visible within the light corridors on the lower-central flank.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A large, pronounced focal protrusion or lump is visible on the upper dorsal-lateral region near the shoulder transition, creating a significant deviation from the expected anatomical contour.
other_distinctive_markers: Presence of multiple small, dark-feathered avian organisms (oxpeckers) perched along the dorsal ridge and upper mane area.
